title: Etiquette & language
body:
Yatai etiquette is real and locally enforced — don't linger once you're done eating (the bench seat is someone else's queue), and expect cash-only. Ryokan etiquette at Miyamaso Takamiya: yukata provided, wear it loosely left-over-right (right-over-left is how the dead are dressed); a no-tattoos policy is common at communal onsen baths in older properties — worth confirming directly with the ryokan if anyone in the pair going has visible ink. Ropeways and gondolas (Mt. Moiwa, Zao) queue in an orderly line; no jaywalking the boarding area.

Language: English signage is solid at stations and chain stores, thinner at small ramen counters, yatai, and rural onsen towns (Zao, Naruko). A translation app with camera-OCR (Google Translate's photo mode) covers menus without English; point-and-show works everywhere. A situational phrase card is in the Trip kit tab — cross-checked against multiple bilingual sources, but a translation app is still the better tool for anything beyond the basics.
